Definition: from G3083; to ransom (literally or figuratively):--redeem.
BiblicalUsage: The word means to redeem, to buy back by paying a price, and the New Testament uses it for what Christ did for His people. On the road to Emmaus the two disciples said they had trusted He was the one who would redeem Israel, and Paul says Christ gave Himself to redeem us from all iniquity, while Peter says we were not redeemed with silver and gold but by His blood.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that redemption is not a figure of speech: we were bought, and the price was Christ Himself, so my life is no longer my own.
